title: Web APIs Quick Guide
description: Find a short explanation and a worked example for each idea in the Web APIs course.

entries.name: Read JSON text
entries.summary: JSON is a text format for data. JSON.parse turns that text into JavaScript values that code can read.

entries.name: Fetch local data
entries.summary: fetch asks for a resource and returns a promise for a response.

entries.name: Stop a request
entries.summary: AbortController gives a request a stop signal.

entries.name: Use URL search values
entries.summary: URLSearchParams reads and writes query values in an address.

entries.name: Remember a small browser value
entries.summary: localStorage stores small text values for one site in one browser.

entries.name: Read a chosen file
entries.summary: A file input lets a person choose a file.

entries.name: Copy text after a click
entries.summary: The Clipboard API can write text to the clipboard.

entries.name: Ask for a location carefully
entries.summary: Geolocation asks the browser for a location.

entries.name: Draw a simple canvas shape
entries.summary: Canvas is a drawing area controlled by JavaScript.

example.code: <canvas id="art" width="240" height="120" aria-label="A blue rectangle">A blue rectangle</canvas><script>const ctx=document.querySelector("#art").getContext("2d");ctx.fillStyle="navy";ctx.fillRect(20,20,100,60);</script>

entries.name: Watch when a part comes into view
entries.summary: IntersectionObserver tells your code when an element crosses a visibility boundary.

entries.summary: A web worker runs JavaScript in another thread.
